html:
The Restoration War was the Dominican struggle from 1863 to 1865 to win back independence after Spain had annexed the country in 1861, at the invitation of President Pedro Santana.

Spanish rule brought new taxes, Spanish officials and fears that slavery would return, since Spain still kept slaves in Cuba and Puerto Rico. Rebels began the war at Capotillo on 16 August 1863, now a national holiday, and fought from the north around Santiago.

Guerrilla war and yellow fever wore down the Spanish army, and Spain withdrew in 1865. The war gave the country its second independence after the break from Haiti, and leaders such as Gregorio Luperon.
